The ride was a metered RydeTAXI trip Marina Bay Sands → Tampines Mall, 20.1 km actual against 15.9 km optimal, 30.6 min against 21 min, $41.62 charged [F1][F2][F6][RD-1]. The trace marks one off-route segment as settled: F3, 08:58–09:05, 4.39 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.64 km, adding 3.75 km and straying up to 1034 m [F3][RD-1]. No exemption applies: no incident was recorded near the route [F13], the two expressway readings are band 4 (30–39 km/h), outside the band 1–2 congestion RD-4 requires and insufficient on their own [F11][F12][RD-4], weather was fair [F14], and the driver's "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" [F10] is a post-trip statement, not consent [RD-5]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped [F9], and the only rider message about the route, at 09:03, objects to it ("Why are we going this way?") — after the segment began at 08:58 — so there is no rider agreement before the segment [F7][F9][RD-5]; nor was any stop named or made, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt it [F3][F7][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as an unexempted detour, and the driver's duty to take the shortest and most direct route was breached [RD-1].

On this metered service the refund follows RD-2: only the extra distance units of the unexempted segment are returned, at the trip's per-km rate taken from the fare fact. The trace fixes the rate at $1.4101/km ($28.30 ÷ 20.1 km) [F6][RD-2], so 3.75 km × $1.4101/km = $5.2879, rounded to $5.29 [F3][F6][RD-2]. Both advocates landed on the same figure, and neither side now disputes liability, so the amount is $5.29.

I cannot, however, release this as an automatic refund. Read in context that is not a neutral driving instruction: it is hostile, demeaning language aimed at silencing the passenger, and Ryde's Code of Conduct bars abuse of any kind, including intimidation of a passenger — that is abuse under SAFE-1 and is therefore at least "suspected" [F8][RD-1][SAFE-1]. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment on this metered RydeTAXI trip (08:58–09:05) in which 4.39 km was driven where the optimal route covers 0.64 km, adding 3.75 km and straying up to 1034 m from the optimal route; total distance was 20.1 km vs 15.9 km optimal (+4.2 km, +26%). Under RD-1 nothing exempts this segment, so it is an unexempted detour in breach of the driver's duty to take the shortest and most direct route.

No reasonable cause exists for the detour: traffic records show no incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window, weather was fair, and the two expressway speed bands recorded (band 4, 30–39 km/h) are far from the band 1–2 congestion levels RD-4 requires, so the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' statement in F10 is not supported by any traffic fact.

The rider never consented to the route change: the only rider message before and during the segment is Chat #1 at 09:03 asking 'Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app' — sent after the detour had already started at 08:58 and objecting to it, not agreeing to it; there is no agreement message before 08:58, so RD-5 does not exempt the segment.

Because this is a RydeTAXI meter fare, the extra distance passed straight into the fare: the unbilled meter effect is the unexempted detour's 3.75 km × the trip's per-km rate ($28.30 distance fare ÷ 20.1 km = $1.4080/km) = $5.28, which the rider should get back under RD-2.

A separate basis for a partial refund is billing: the fare charged $28.30 of distance for 20.1 km, i.e. $5.91 of distance fare above the 15.9 km optimal route, and no surcharge or extra published item accounts for the 4.2 km / 9.2 extra minutes beyond published waiting/platform fees (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge), so the excess on the unexempted segment is not a fare the rider owes.

The driver's reply 'Shut up and let me drive' (Chat #2, 09:04) after the rider's question is verbal abuse/harassment of a passenger and an intimidation of the rider who was questioning the route; the complaint also states the rider 'felt unsafe', so the case must go to a person rather than be decided automatically.
No account flag is warranted here: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld dispute in the last 90 days, so the RD-6 precondition of route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 additional to this case is not met.

weaknesses: My refund figure is a derivation, not a fact-table line: RD-2 amounts the refund for non-metered services but for RydeTAXI it uses extra_km × per-km rate, and the per-km rate must be derived from F6 ($28.30 ÷ 20.1 km); the driver will argue the whole 4.2 km gap (F4's $5.91) is the measure, or that no figure is computable at all.
The detour already had a meter running, so the driver can argue the rider would have paid most of the fare regardless of route; my $5.28 claim is only the incremental distance, not the whole $41.62.

The driver's F10 claim of a GPS reroute plus the recorded expressway band 4 (30–39 km/h) speeds (F11, F12) will be used to argue ordinary traffic, and RD-4(b) says band data alone is not enough to exempt — but the judge may still read it as mitigating.

There was no rider stop request to analyse under RD-3, and my consent argument (C3) rests on the absence of a pre-08:58 message — the driver may argue the initial lack of objection implied acceptance, though RD-5/G11 require an actual message from the rider before the segment.
The rider's own profile shows 2 disputes in the last 90 days with 0 upheld (F15), which the driver may use to paint this as a repeat unfounded complaint.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (fare breakdown base $3.90 + distance $28.30 @ $1.41/km + time $7.95, total $41.62), so under RD-2 only the distance units of exempt-less segments can be refunded, at most 3.75 km × $1.41 = $5.29, and the rider's demand for the whole fare fails.

No exemption under RD-4 is available: LTA traffic facts record no incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window (F13), and the only conditions recorded are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and KPE — well outside bands 1–2 — so the reroute was not caused by road closure, accident or severe congestion.

The driver's post-trip statement that 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a statement, not consent and not an exemption; no message in the chat shows the rider agreeing to any route change before the segment began, so RD-5 consent does not apply to the 08:58–09:05 segment.

Conversely, the rider's own message at 09:03 asking 'Why are we going this way?' (F7) came after the deviation had already started at 08:58, and the rider never named an alternative stop or destination; nothing in the chat requests or approves the detour route, so no rider-directed stop under RD-3 mitigates it either.

The complaint's 'he told me to shut up' is a rude, unpleasant remark (chat #2, 09:04) but it is not a threat, intimidation or harassment directed at the rider's safety, and the rider's 'felt unsafe' adds no allegation of a dangerous driving act, so the case should stay with the automatic route finding rather than being escalated under SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

No refund larger than the metered distance value of the unexempted segment is computable from the fare facts: the excess-distance line is $5.91 for 4.2 km (F4) and the segment's own extra km is 3.75 km × $1.41 = $5.29, so any award should be capped at $5.29 and the customer's remaining $36.33 of base, time, platform and legitimate distance stands.

weaknesses: The 08:58–09:05 segment is a real off-route segment with 3.75 km extra (F3), and the trip ran 20.1 km against a 15.9 km optimal route (+26%) in 30.6 min vs 21 min (F1, F2) — RD-1 is breached and RD-2 will produce a refund that I cannot argue down to zero.

The traffic facts are bad for us: F13 records no incidents at all near the route, and F11/F12 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and KPE, which is insufficient under RD-4(a) and cannot exempt the segment even as corroboration under RD-4(b).

I do not contest this point: F13 records no incidents near the route, F14 records fair weather with 0.0 mm rain, and F11/F12 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and KPE, which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment alone; F10 is a driver statement, not traffic corroboration, and my D4 already treats it as such.
